paragraphs.text: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
paragraphs.original: Οὗτος γὰρ ὁ Μελχισέδεκ, βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ, ἱερεὺς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου, ὁ συναντήσας Ἀβραὰμ ὑποστρέφοντι ἀπὸ τῆς κοπῆς τῶν βασιλέων καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτόν,
paragraphs.translit: Houtos gar ho Melchisedek, basileus Salēm, hiereus tou theou tou hypsistou, ho synantēsas Abraam hypostrephonti apo tēs kopēs tōn basileōn kai eulogēsas auton,

paragraphs.text: to whom also Abraham divided a tenth part of all (being first, by interpretation, King of righteousness, and then also King of Salem, which is King of peace;
paragraphs.original: ᾧ καὶ δεκάτην ἀπὸ πάντων ἐμέρισεν Ἀβραάμ, πρῶτον μὲν ἑρμηνευόμενος βασιλεὺς δικαιοσύνης ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ, ὅ ἐστιν βασιλεὺς εἰρήνης,
paragraphs.translit: hō kai dekatēn apo pantōn emerisen Abraam, prōton men hermēneuomenos basileus dikaiosynēs epeita de kai basileus Salēm, ho estin basileus eirēnēs,

paragraphs.text: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like unto the Son of God), abideth a priest continually.
paragraphs.original: ἀπάτωρ, ἀμήτωρ, ἀγενεαλόγητος, μήτε ἀρχὴν ἡμερῶν μήτε ζωῆς τέλος ἔχων, ἀφωμοιωμένος δὲ τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ θεοῦ, μένει ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸ διηνεκές.
paragraphs.translit: apatōr, amētōr, agenealogētos, mēte archēn hēmerōn mēte zōēs telos echōn, aphōmoiōmenos de tō hyiō tou theou, menei hiereus eis to diēnekes.

paragraphs.text: Now consider how great this man was, unto whom Abraham, the patriarch, gave a tenth out of the chief spoils.
paragraphs.original: Θεωρεῖτε δὲ πηλίκος οὗτος ᾧ δεκάτην Ἀβραὰμ ἔδωκεν ἐκ τῶν ἀκροθινίων ὁ πατριάρχης.
paragraphs.translit: Theōreite de pēlikos houtos hō dekatēn Abraam edōken ek tōn akrothiniōn ho patriarchēs.

paragraphs.text: And they indeed of the sons of Levi that receive the priest`s office have commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though these have come out of the loins of Abraham:
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐκ τῶν υἱῶν Λευὶ τὴν ἱερατείαν λαμβάνοντες ἐντολὴν ἔχουσιν ἀποδεκατοῦν τὸν λαὸν κατὰ τὸν νόμον, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτῶν, καίπερ ἐξεληλυθότας ἐκ τῆς ὀσφύος Ἀβραάμ·
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi men ek tōn hyiōn Leui tēn hierateian lambanontes entolēn echousin apodekatoun ton laon kata ton nomon, toutʼ estin tous adelphous autōn, kaiper exelēlythotas ek tēs osphyos Abraam·

paragraphs.text: but he whose genealogy is not counted from them hath taken tithes of Abraham, and hath blessed him that hath the promises.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ μὴ γενεαλογούμενος ἐξ αὐτῶν δεδεκάτωκεν Ἀβραάμ, καὶ τὸν ἔχοντα τὰς ἐπαγγελίας εὐλόγηκεν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de mē genealogoumenos ex autōn dedekatōken Abraam, kai ton echonta tas epangelias eulogēken.

paragraphs.text: But without any dispute the less is blessed of the better.
paragraphs.original: χωρὶς δὲ πάσης ἀντιλογίας τὸ ἔλαττον ὑπὸ τοῦ κρείττονος εὐλογεῖται.
paragraphs.translit: chōris de pasēs antilogias to elatton hypo tou kreittonos eulogeitai.

paragraphs.text: And here men that die receive tithes; but there one, of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὧδε μὲν δεκάτας ἀποθνῄσκοντες ἄνθρωποι λαμβάνουσιν, ἐκεῖ δὲ μαρτυρούμενος ὅτι ζῇ.
paragraphs.translit: kai hōde men dekatas apothnēskontes anthrōpoi lambanousin, ekei de martyroumenos hoti zē.

paragraphs.text: And, so to say, through Abraham even Levi, who receiveth tithes, hath paid tithes;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, διʼ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Λευὶ ὁ δεκάτας λαμβάνων δεδεκάτωται,
paragraphs.translit: kai hōs epos eipein, diʼ Abraam kai Leui ho dekatas lambanōn dedekatōtai,

paragraphs.text: for he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchizedek met him.
paragraphs.original: ἔτι γὰρ ἐν τῇ ὀσφύϊ τοῦ πατρὸς ἦν ὅτε συνήντησεν αὐτῷ Μελχισέδεκ.
paragraphs.translit: eti gar en tē osphyi tou patros ēn hote synēntēsen autō Melchisedek.

paragraphs.text: Now if there was perfection through the Levitical priesthood (for under it hath the people received the law), what further need [was there] that another priest should arise after the order of Melchizedek, and not be reckoned after the order of Aaron?
paragraphs.original: Εἰ μὲν οὖν τελείωσις διὰ τῆς Λευιτικῆς ἱερωσύνης ἦν, ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἐπʼ αὐτῆς νενομοθέτηται, τίς ἔτι χρεία κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἕτερον ἀνίστασθαι ἱερέα καὶ οὐ κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Ἀαρὼν λέγεσθαι;
paragraphs.translit: Ei men oun teleiōsis dia tēs Leuitikēs hierōsynēs ēn, ho laos gar epʼ autēs nenomothetētai, tis eti chreia kata tēn taxin Melchisedek heteron anistasthai hierea kai ou kata tēn taxin Aarōn legesthai;

paragraphs.text: For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.
paragraphs.original: μετατιθεμένης γὰρ τῆς ἱερωσύνης ἐξ ἀνάγκης καὶ νόμου μετάθεσις γίνεται.
paragraphs.translit: metatithemenēs gar tēs hierōsynēs ex anankēs kai nomou metathesis ginetai.

paragraphs.text: For he of whom these things are said belongeth to another tribe, from which no man hath given attendance at the altar.
paragraphs.original: ἐφʼ ὃν γὰρ λέγεται ταῦτα φυλῆς ἑτέρας μετέσχηκεν, ἀφʼ ἧς οὐδεὶς προσέσχηκεν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ·
paragraphs.translit: ephʼ hon gar legetai tauta phylēs heteras meteschēken, aphʼ hēs oudeis proseschēken tō thysiastēriō·

paragraphs.text: For it is evident that our Lord hath sprung out of Judah; as to which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priests.
paragraphs.original: πρόδηλον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξ Ἰούδα ἀνατέταλκεν ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν, εἰς ἣν φυλὴν περὶ ἱερέων οὐδὲν Μωϋσῆς ἐλάλησεν.
paragraphs.translit: prodēlon gar hoti ex Iouda anatetalken ho kyrios hēmōn, eis hēn phylēn peri hiereōn ouden Mōysēs elalēsen.

paragraphs.text: And [what we say] is yet more abundantly evident, if after the likeness of Melchizedek there ariseth another priest,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ περισσότερον ἔτι κατάδηλόν ἐστιν, εἰ κατὰ τὴν ὁμοιότητα Μελχισέδεκ ἀνίσταται ἱερεὺς ἕτερος,
paragraphs.translit: Kai perissoteron eti katadēlon estin, ei kata tēn homoiotēta Melchisedek anistatai hiereus heteros,

paragraphs.text: who hath been made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life:
paragraphs.original: ὃς οὐ κατὰ νόμον ἐντολῆς σαρκίνης γέγονεν ἀλλὰ κατὰ δύναμιν ζωῆς ἀκαταλύτου,
paragraphs.translit: hos ou kata nomon entolēs sarkinēs gegonen alla kata dynamin zōēs akatalytou,

paragraphs.text: for it is witnessed [of him,] Thou art a priest for ever After the order of Melchizedek.
paragraphs.original: μαρτυρεῖται γὰρ ὅτι Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ.
paragraphs.translit: martyreitai gar hoti Sy hiereus eis ton aiōna kata tēn taxin Melchisedek.

paragraphs.text: For there is a disannulling of a foregoing commandment because of its weakness and unprofitableness
paragraphs.original: ἀθέτησις μὲν γὰρ γίνεται προαγούσης ἐντολῆς διὰ τὸ αὐτῆς ἀσθενὲς καὶ ἀνωφελές,
paragraphs.translit: athetēsis men gar ginetai proagousēs entolēs dia to autēs asthenes kai anōpheles,

paragraphs.text: (for the law made nothing perfect), and a bringing in thereupon of a better hope, through which we draw nigh unto God.
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐτελείωσεν ὁ νόμος, ἐπεισαγωγὴ δὲ κρείττονος ἐλπίδος, διʼ ἧς ἐγγίζομεν τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ouden gar eteleiōsen ho nomos, epeisagōgē de kreittonos elpidos, diʼ hēs engizomen tō theō.

paragraphs.text: And inasmuch as [it is] not without the taking of an oath
paragraphs.original: Καὶ καθʼ ὅσον οὐ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας (οἱ μὲν γὰρ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας εἰσὶν ἱερεῖς γεγονότες,
paragraphs.translit: Kai kathʼ hoson ou chōris horkōmosias (hoi men gar chōris horkōmosias eisin hiereis gegonotes,

paragraphs.text: (for they indeed have been made priests without an oath; but he with an oath by him that saith of him, The Lord sware and will not repent himself, Thou art a priest for ever);
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ μετὰ ὁρκωμοσίας διὰ τοῦ λέγοντος πρὸς αὐτόν· Ὤμοσεν κύριος, καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται, Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα),
paragraphs.translit: ho de meta horkōmosias dia tou legontos pros auton· Ōmosen kyrios, kai ou metamelēthēsetai, Sy hiereus eis ton aiōna),

paragraphs.text: by so much also hath Jesus become the surety of a better covenant.
paragraphs.original: κατὰ τοσοῦτο κρείττονος διαθήκης γέγονεν ἔγγυος Ἰησοῦς.
paragraphs.translit: kata tosouto kreittonos diathēkēs gegonen engyos Iēsous.

paragraphs.text: And they indeed have been made priests many in number, because that by death they are hindered from continuing:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ οἱ μὲν πλείονές εἰσιν γεγονότες ἱερεῖς διὰ τὸ θανάτῳ κωλύεσθαι παραμένειν·
paragraphs.translit: Kai hoi men pleiones eisin gegonotes hiereis dia to thanatō kōlyesthai paramenein·

paragraphs.text: but he, because he abideth for ever, hath his priesthood unchangeable.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ διὰ τὸ μένειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἀπαράβατον ἔχει τὴν ἱερωσύνην·
paragraphs.translit: ho de dia to menein auton eis ton aiōna aparabaton echei tēn hierōsynēn·

paragraphs.text: Wherefore also he is able to save to the uttermost them that draw near unto God through him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
paragraphs.original: ὅθεν καὶ σῴζειν εἰς τὸ παντελὲς δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους διʼ αὐτοῦ τῷ θεῷ, πάντοτε ζῶν εἰς τὸ ἐντυγχάνειν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hothen kai sōzein eis to panteles dynatai tous proserchomenous diʼ autou tō theō, pantote zōn eis to entynchanein hyper autōn.

paragraphs.text: For such a high priest became us, holy, guileless, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
paragraphs.original: Τοιοῦτος γὰρ ἡμῖν καὶ ἔπρεπεν ἀρχιερεύς, ὅσιος, ἄκακος, ἀμίαντος, κεχωρισμένος ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν, καὶ ὑψηλότερος τῶν οὐρανῶν γενόμενος·
paragraphs.translit: Toioutos gar hēmin kai eprepen archiereus, hosios, akakos, amiantos, kechōrismenos apo tōn hamartōlōn, kai hypsēloteros tōn ouranōn genomenos·

paragraphs.text: who needeth not daily, like those high priests, to offer up sacrifices, first for his own sins, and then for the [sins] of the people: for this he did once for all, when he offered up himself.
paragraphs.original: ὃς οὐκ ἔχει καθʼ ἡμέραν ἀνάγκην, ὥσπερ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς, πρότερον ὑπὲρ τῶν ἰδίων ἁμαρτιῶν θυσίας ἀναφέρειν, ἔπειτα τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ (τοῦτο γὰρ ἐποίησεν ἐφάπαξ ἑαυτὸν ἀνενέγκας)·
paragraphs.translit: hos ouk echei kathʼ hēmeran anankēn, hōsper hoi archiereis, proteron hyper tōn idiōn hamartiōn thysias anapherein, epeita tōn tou laou (touto gar epoiēsen ephapax heauton anenenkas)·

paragraphs.text: For the law appointeth men high priests, having infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was after the law, [appointeth] a Son, perfected for evermore.
paragraphs.original: ὁ νόμος γὰρ ἀνθρώπους καθίστησιν ἀρχιερεῖς ἔχοντας ἀσθένειαν, ὁ λόγος δὲ τῆς ὁρκωμοσίας τῆς μετὰ τὸν νόμον υἱόν, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τετελειωμένον.
paragraphs.translit: ho nomos gar anthrōpous kathistēsin archiereis echontas astheneian, ho logos de tēs horkōmosias tēs meta ton nomon hyion, eis ton aiōna teteleiōmenon.
